sw.B: ikiwa nimelitazama jua lilipong'aa, \q au mwezi ukienda katika fahari yake,
sw.R: Je, nimeliangalia jua linalong'aa \q au mwezi unaong'aa ukipita angani,

vi.L: nếu tôi đã nhìn ánh sáng khi nó chiếu rạng, \q hoặc mặt trăng đi trong vẻ huy hoàng,
vi.B: nếu tôi đã ngắm mặt trời khi nó chiếu sáng, \q hoặc mặt trăng di chuyển trong vẻ huy hoàng,
vi.R: Tôi có ngước nhìn mặt trời chói lọi \q hay mặt trăng sáng ngời đi ngang bầu trời,

ko.L: 만일 내가 빛이 비칠 때에 그것을 보았거나 \q 달이 찬란하게 지나가는 것을 보고,
ko.B: 만일 내가 해가 빛날 때에 그것을 바라보았거나 \q 달이 찬란하게 떠가는 것을 바라보고,
ko.R: 내가 빛나는 해나 \q 하늘을 지나가는 밝은 달을 쳐다보고,

pt.L: se olhei para a luz quando brilhava, \q ou para a lua que caminhava em esplendor,
pt.B: se olhei para o sol quando brilhava, \q ou para a lua que avançava no seu esplendor,
pt.R: Por acaso olhei para o sol brilhante \q ou para a lua clara atravessando o céu,

decisions.choice: the light: the sun
decisions.reason: Set beside the moon, "the light" is the sun (as in 37:21 and Genesis 1:16, "the greater light").

decisions.choice: looking at sun and moon: being drawn to worship them
decisions.reason: Worship of the sun and moon was common in the ancient world, and Israel's law forbade it (Deuteronomy 4:19; 17:3; 2 Kings 23:5; Ezekiel 8:16). "Looked at" here is the gaze of admiration that leads to worship, as verse 27 shows.

decisions.choice: the sun
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "sun" for "the light" (m1); Literal keeps "the light".

source.text: וַיִּ֣פְתְּ בַּסֵּ֣תֶר לִבִּ֑י וַתִּשַּׁ֖ק יָדִ֣י לְפִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: and was enticed in secret my heart, and kissed my hand to my mouth,

en.L: and my heart has been secretly enticed, \q and my hand has kissed my mouth,
en.B: and my heart has been secretly enticed, \q so that I threw them a kiss with my hand,
en.R: and been secretly tempted to worship them? \q Have I blown them a kiss with my hand?

es.L: y mi corazón ha sido seducido en secreto, \q y mi mano ha besado mi boca,
es.B: y mi corazón se ha dejado seducir en secreto, \q de modo que les he lanzado un beso con la mano,
es.R: y he sentido en secreto la tentación de adorarlos? \q ¿Les he lanzado un beso con la mano?

fr.L: et que mon cœur a été séduit en secret, \q et que ma main a baisé ma bouche,
fr.B: et que mon cœur s’est laissé séduire en secret, \q au point de leur envoyer un baiser de la main,
fr.R: et ai-je été tenté en secret de les adorer ? \q Leur ai-je envoyé un baiser de la main ?

sw.L: na moyo wangu umeshawishiwa kwa siri, \q na mkono wangu umebusu kinywa changu,
sw.B: na moyo wangu umeshawishiwa kwa siri, \q hata nikavirushia busu kwa mkono wangu,
sw.R: na kujaribiwa kwa siri kuviabudu? \q Je, nimevirushia busu kwa mkono wangu?

vi.L: và lòng tôi đã bị quyến dụ cách kín đáo, \q và tay tôi đã hôn miệng tôi,
vi.B: và lòng tôi đã thầm bị quyến dụ, \q đến nỗi lấy tay gửi cho chúng một nụ hôn,
vi.R: và thầm bị cám dỗ thờ lạy chúng không? \q Tôi có lấy tay gửi cho chúng một nụ hôn không?

ko.L: 내 마음이 남몰래 꾀임을 받아 \q 내 손이 내 입에 입 맞추었다면,
ko.B: 내 마음이 남몰래 유혹을 받아 \q 손으로 그것들에게 입맞춤을 보냈다면,
ko.R: 남몰래 그것들을 섬기고 싶은 유혹을 받았느냐? \q 손으로 그것들에게 입맞춤을 보냈느냐?

pt.L: e o meu coração foi seduzido em segredo, \q e a minha mão beijou a minha boca,
pt.B: e o meu coração foi seduzido em segredo, \q a ponto de eu lhes mandar um beijo com a mão,
pt.R: e senti em segredo vontade de adorá-los? \q Mandei um beijo para eles com a mão?

decisions.choice: my hand has kissed my mouth: a kiss thrown as an act of worship
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says the hand kissed (or was kissed) at the mouth: the worshiper kissed his hand and held it out toward the sun or moon. Kissing was a gesture of worship toward idols (1 Kings 19:18; Hosea 13:2).

decisions.choice: secretly enticed: privately drawn in
decisions.reason: The same verb as in verse 9 (patah). Even a hidden, inward turning to the heavenly lights would be a betrayal of God (verse 28).

decisions.choice: threw them a kiss (B), blown them a kiss (R)
alternatives: my hand has kissed my mouth
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say in English what the gesture was (m1); Literal keeps "my hand has kissed my mouth".

decisions.choice: tempted to worship them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the heart was enticed to do (m2; verse 26, m2).

source.text: גַּם־ה֭וּאעָוֺ֣ן פְּלִילִ֑י כִּֽי־כִחַ֖שְׁתִּי לָאֵ֣ל מִמָּֽעַל׃

records.literal_gloss: Also that [is an] iniquity [for] judges, for I would have denied God from above.

en.L: that also [would be] an iniquity [for] judges, \q for I would have denied God above.
en.B: this too would be a crime to be punished by the judges, \q for I would have been false to God above.
en.R: If I had, that would be a crime that judges should punish. \q I would have turned my back on God in heaven.

es.L: también eso [sería] una iniquidad [para] jueces, \q porque habría negado al Dios de arriba.
es.B: también esto sería un crimen que los jueces deben castigar, \q porque habría sido infiel al Dios de lo alto.
es.R: Si lo hubiera hecho, sería un delito que los jueces deberían castigar. \q Le habría dado la espalda al Dios del cielo.

fr.L: cela aussi [serait] une iniquité [pour les] juges, \q car j’aurais renié le Dieu d’en haut.
fr.B: cela aussi serait un crime que les juges doivent punir, \q car j’aurais été infidèle au Dieu d’en haut.
fr.R: Si je l’avais fait, ce serait un crime que les juges devraient punir. \q J’aurais tourné le dos au Dieu du ciel.

sw.L: hilo nalo [lingekuwa] hatia [mbele ya] waamuzi, \q kwa maana ningekuwa nimemkana Mungu aliye juu.
sw.B: hili nalo lingekuwa kosa linalostahili kuadhibiwa na waamuzi, \q kwa maana ningekuwa sikumwamini Mungu aliye juu.
sw.R: Kama ningefanya hivyo, lingekuwa kosa ambalo waamuzi wangepaswa kuliadhibu. \q Ningekuwa nimempa kisogo Mungu aliye mbinguni.

vi.L: điều đó cũng [là] tội [đáng bị] quan án [xét xử], \q vì tôi đã chối bỏ Đức Chúa Trời trên cao.
vi.B: điều này cũng sẽ là tội đáng bị các quan án trừng phạt, \q vì tôi đã bất trung với Đức Chúa Trời trên cao.
vi.R: Nếu có, đó là tội mà các quan án phải trừng phạt. \q Tôi đã quay lưng lại với Đức Chúa Trời trên trời.

ko.L: 그것 또한 재판관들[이 다스릴] 죄악[이다]. \q 내가 위에 계신 하나님을 부인한 것이기 때문이다.
ko.B: 이것 또한 재판관들에게 벌을 받아야 할 죄악이다. \q 내가 위에 계신 하나님을 저버린 것이 되기 때문이다.
ko.R: 만일 그랬다면, 그것은 재판관들이 벌해야 할 범죄다. \q 나는 하늘에 계신 하나님께 등을 돌린 것이다.

pt.L: também isso [seria] uma iniquidade [para os] juízes, \q pois eu teria negado o Deus lá de cima.
pt.B: também isso seria um delito a ser punido pelos juízes, \q pois eu teria sido infiel ao Deus lá do alto.
pt.R: Se fiz isso, seria um crime que os juízes deveriam punir. \q Eu teria dado as costas para o Deus do céu.

decisions.choice: an iniquity for judges: a crime for the courts
decisions.reason: The phrase is the same as in verse 11, with an adjective form of the word for judges. Worship of other gods was a crime under the law (Deuteronomy 17:2-7).

decisions.choice: denied: been false to, disowned
decisions.reason: The verb (kichesh) means to deny or deal falsely with someone (Joshua 24:27; Proverbs 30:9). Trusting in gold or worshiping the sky would disown God, who is above all of them.

decisions.choice: God: the word 'El
decisions.reason: 'El, rendered "God".

decisions.choice: If I had; turned my back on
decisions.reason: Readable gives the verdict after its questions (verse 5, r-en-1) and says "turned my back on" for "denied" (m2).

decisions.choice: uma iniquidade [para os] juízes (L); um delito a ser punido pelos juízes (B), as in verse 11
decisions.reason: The phrase repeats verse 11 (m1), so each level uses the same words in both verses and the reader hears that idolatry is judged like adultery.

source.text: אִם־אֶ֭שְׂמַח בְּפִ֣יד מְשַׂנְאִ֑י וְ֝הִתְעֹרַ֗רְתִּי כִּֽי־מְצָ֥אוֹ רָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: If I rejoiced at [the] ruin of [one] hating me, and I roused myself when found him evil,

en.L: If I have rejoiced at the ruin of one who hated me, \q or exulted when evil found him,
en.B: If I have rejoiced at the ruin of someone who hated me, \q or gloated when disaster overtook them,
en.R: Have I been glad when someone who hated me was ruined? \q Have I gloated when trouble came to them?

es.L: Si me he alegrado de la ruina del que me odiaba, \q o me he regocijado cuando el mal lo alcanzó,
es.B: Si me he alegrado de la ruina de alguien que me odiaba, \q o me he regodeado cuando la desgracia lo alcanzó,
es.R: ¿Me he alegrado cuando alguien que me odiaba quedó arruinado? \q ¿Me he burlado cuando le llegaron los problemas?

fr.L: Si je me suis réjoui de la ruine de celui qui me haïssait, \q ou si j’ai exulté quand le mal l’a atteint,
fr.B: Si je me suis réjoui de la ruine de quelqu’un qui me haïssait, \q ou si j’ai jubilé quand le malheur l’a frappé,
fr.R: Ai-je été content quand quelqu’un qui me haïssait a été ruiné ? \q Me suis-je réjoui méchamment quand les ennuis l’ont frappé ?

sw.L: Ikiwa nimefurahia maangamizi ya anayenichukia, \q au nimeshangilia uovu ulipompata,
sw.B: Ikiwa nimefurahia maangamizi ya mtu aliyenichukia, \q au nimejigamba maafa yalipompata,
sw.R: Je, nimefurahi mtu aliyenichukia alipoangamia? \q Je, nimeshangilia taabu zilipomjia?

vi.L: Nếu tôi đã vui mừng vì sự sụp đổ của kẻ ghét tôi, \q hoặc hớn hở khi tai họa đến với hắn,
vi.B: Nếu tôi đã vui mừng khi kẻ ghét tôi bị suy sụp, \q hoặc hả hê khi tai ương ập xuống trên hắn,
vi.R: Tôi có vui khi người ghét tôi bị khốn đốn không? \q Tôi có hả hê khi người ấy gặp hoạn nạn không?

ko.L: 만일 내가 나를 미워하는 자의 멸망을 기뻐했거나 \q 재앙이 그에게 닥쳤을 때 우쭐했다면,
ko.B: 만일 내가 나를 미워하는 사람이 망한 것을 기뻐했거나 \q 재난이 그를 덮쳤을 때 고소해했다면,
ko.R: 나를 미워하는 사람이 망했을 때 내가 기뻐했느냐? \q 그에게 어려움이 닥쳤을 때 고소해했느냐?

pt.L: Se me alegrei com a ruína de quem me odiava, \q ou exultei quando o mal o atingiu,
pt.B: Se me alegrei com a ruína de alguém que me odiava, \q ou me regozijei quando a desgraça o alcançou,
pt.R: Por acaso fiquei contente quando alguém que me odiava se arruinou? \q Fiquei feliz quando a desgraça chegou para essa pessoa?

decisions.choice: not rejoicing over an enemy's fall
decisions.reason: Proverbs forbids gloating when an enemy falls (Proverbs 24:17), and the law commands help for an enemy's animal (Exodus 23:4-5). Job swears that he kept even his heart free of such joy.

decisions.choice: exulted: was roused to glee
decisions.reason: The verb ('ur, in a reflexive form) means to stir oneself up, here to be excited with delight.

decisions.choice: if without a curse: an oath that he did not
decisions.reason: No curse follows this "if"; verse 30 breaks in instead. As in verse 5, "if" in an oath then means "I swear I did not".

decisions.choice: someone ... them
decisions.reason: The enemy may be anyone, so Balanced and Readable say "someone" and "them"; Literal keeps "him".

source.text: וְלֹא־נָתַ֣תִּי לַחֲטֹ֣א חִכִּ֑י לִשְׁאֹ֖ל בְּאָלָ֣ה נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And not have I given to sin my palate, by asking with a curse his life.

en.L: And I have not let my palate sin \q by asking for his life with a curse.
en.B: I have not let my mouth sin \q by calling down a curse on their life.
en.R: No, I have never let my mouth sin \q by cursing them and wishing them dead.

es.L: Y no he dejado pecar a mi paladar \q pidiendo con maldición su vida.
es.B: No he dejado que mi boca peque \q lanzando una maldición contra su vida.
es.R: No, nunca he dejado que mi boca peque \q maldiciéndolo y deseándole la muerte.

fr.L: Et je n’ai pas permis à mon palais de pécher \q en demandant sa vie par une malédiction.
fr.B: Je n’ai pas laissé ma bouche pécher \q en appelant la malédiction sur sa vie.
fr.R: Non, je n’ai jamais laissé ma bouche pécher \q en le maudissant et en souhaitant sa mort.

sw.L: Wala sikuliacha kaakaa langu litende dhambi \q kwa kuuomba uhai wake kwa laana.
sw.B: Sikukiacha kinywa changu kitende dhambi \q kwa kuuombea uhai wake laana.
sw.R: Hapana, sijawahi kukiacha kinywa changu kitende dhambi \q kwa kumlaani na kumtakia kifo.

vi.L: Và tôi đã không để vòm miệng tôi phạm tội \q bằng cách lấy lời nguyền rủa mà đòi mạng sống hắn.
vi.B: Tôi chẳng để miệng mình phạm tội \q bằng cách rủa sả mạng sống của hắn.
vi.R: Không, tôi chưa bao giờ để miệng mình phạm tội \q bằng cách nguyền rủa người ấy, mong cho người ấy chết.

ko.L: 나는 내 입천장이 죄를 짓게 하지 않았고 \q 저주로 그의 목숨을 구하지 않았다.
ko.B: 나는 내 입이 죄를 짓게 하지 않았고 \q 그의 목숨에 저주를 빌지 않았다.
ko.R: 아니다, 나는 내 입으로 죄를 지은 적이 없다. \q 그를 저주하며 죽기를 바란 적이 없다.

pt.L: E não deixei o meu paladar pecar \q pedindo a vida dele com uma maldição.
pt.B: Não deixei a minha boca pecar \q lançando uma maldição contra a vida dele.
pt.R: Não! Eu nunca deixei a minha boca pecar \q amaldiçoando essa pessoa e desejando a sua morte.

decisions.choice: Job breaks into the oath with a plain statement
decisions.reason: Instead of a curse on himself, Job states outright that he has not done it, and goes further: he did not even speak against the enemy.

decisions.choice: palate: mouth, speech
decisions.reason: The palate stands for what one says (6:30; Proverbs 8:7).

decisions.choice: asking for his life with a curse: wishing him dead with a spoken curse
decisions.reason: A curse ('alah) was a spoken call for harm. To "ask for his life" by it is to call down death on him (compare 1 Kings 3:11).

decisions.choice: mouth; their (B), them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "mouth" for "palate" (m2), and keep the enemy of verse 29 as "them".

source.text: אִם־לֹ֣א אָ֭מְרוּ מְתֵ֣י אָהֳלִ֑י מִֽי־יִתֵּ֥ן מִ֝בְּשָׂר֗וֹ לֹ֣א נִשְׂבָּֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: If not have said [the] men of my tent, "Who can give from his meat [one] not satisfied?"

en.L: If the men of my tent have not said, \q "Who can find [one] not filled with his meat?"
en.B: If the {{gender:people|men}} of my household have not said, \q "Who has not had their fill of his meat?"
en.R: The {{gender:people|men}} of my household have always said, \q "Everyone has eaten all the meat they wanted at Job's table."

es.L: Si los hombres de mi tienda no han dicho: \q «¿Quién encontrará [a alguien] que no se haya saciado de su carne?»,
es.B: Si {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} de mi casa no han dicho: \q «¿Quién no se ha saciado de su carne?»,
es.R: {{gender:Las personas|Los hombres}} de mi casa siempre han dicho: \q «Todos han comido en la mesa de Job toda la carne que han querido».

fr.L: Si les hommes de ma tente n’ont pas dit : \q « Qui trouvera [quelqu’un] qui ne se soit pas rassasié de sa viande ? »,
fr.B: Si {{gender:les gens|les hommes}} de ma maison n’ont pas dit : \q « Qui n’a pas été rassasié de sa viande ? »,
fr.R: {{gender:Les gens|Les hommes}} de ma maison ont toujours dit : \q « Tout le monde a mangé autant de viande qu’il voulait à la table de Job. »

sw.L: Ikiwa watu wa hema langu hawajasema, \q "Ni nani awezaye kumpata [mtu] asiyeshiba nyama yake?"
sw.B: Ikiwa watu wa nyumbani mwangu hawajasema, \q "Ni nani ambaye hajashiba nyama yake?"
sw.R: Watu wa nyumbani mwangu wamekuwa wakisema daima, \q "Kila mtu amekula nyama aliyotaka mezani pa Ayubu."

vi.L: Nếu những người trong trại tôi đã không nói: \q "Ai tìm được [người nào] chưa được no nê thịt của ông ấy?"
vi.B: Nếu những người trong nhà tôi đã không nói: \q "Có ai chưa được ăn thịt của ông ấy no nê đâu?"
vi.R: Những người trong nhà tôi vẫn luôn nói: \q "Ai đến bàn ăn của ông Gióp cũng được ăn thịt thỏa thích."

ko.L: 만일 내 장막의 사람들이 \q "그의 고기로 배부르지 않은 [사람을] 누가 찾을 수 있겠느냐?" 하고 말하지 않았다면,
ko.B: 만일 내 집안 사람들이 \q "그의 고기를 배불리 먹지 않은 사람이 누가 있느냐?" 하고 말하지 않았다면,
ko.R: 내 집안 사람들은 언제나 \q "누구든지 욥의 상에서 고기를 실컷 먹었다" 하고 말했다.

pt.L: Se os homens da minha tenda não disseram: \q "Quem acharia [alguém] que não se fartou da carne dele?"
pt.B: Se {{gender:as pessoas|os homens}} da minha casa não disseram: \q "Quem não se fartou da carne dele?"
pt.R: {{gender:As pessoas|Os homens}} da minha casa sempre disseram: \q "Todo mundo comeu toda a carne que quis na mesa de Jó."

decisions.choice: if not: an oath that they did say it
decisions.reason: As in verse 20, "if ... not" in an oath means "I swear that it is so": the people of Job's house did say this.

decisions.choice: who can give one not filled: there is no one who has not been fed
alternatives: Oh that we had some of his meat!
decisions.reason: The question "who can give (that is, find) someone not filled with his meat?" means that everyone was fed. Meat was a sign of a generous table, since most people ate it rarely. Verse 32 gives the same picture of hospitality.

decisions.choice: the men of my tent: the members of my household
decisions.reason: The word (metim) means men, people. "My tent" is Job's household, its servants and dependants, as in 19:15 and 29:4.

decisions.choice: people / men of my household
decisions.reason: The household who spoke would have been men and women, so Balanced and Readable use the gender setting; Literal keeps "men", the word's own meaning.

decisions.choice: have always said; a statement in place of the question; Job's table
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain meaning of the oath and the question (m1, m2), and names Job for "his" since the quoted words speak of him.

decisions.choice: {{gender:las personas|los hombres}} de mi casa
decisions.reason: The English has a gender setting here; the household includes women, and Spanish has two wordings, so the span follows the English. Literal keeps "los hombres" for metim.

decisions.choice: {{gender:les gens|les hommes}} de ma maison
decisions.reason: The English has a gender setting here and French has two wordings; Literal keeps « les hommes » for metim.

source.text: בַּ֭חוּץ לֹא־יָלִ֣ין גֵּ֑ר דְּ֝לָתַ֗י לָאֹ֥רַח אֶפְתָּֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: In the street not lodged a sojourner; my doors to the traveler I opened.

en.L: The sojourner did not lodge in the street; \q I opened my doors to the traveler.
en.B: No outsider had to spend the night in the street, \q for I opened my doors to the traveler.
en.R: No stranger ever had to sleep outside in the street. \q I always opened my doors to travelers.

es.L: El forastero no pasaba la noche en la calle; \q mis puertas abría al viajero.
es.B: Ningún extranjero tenía que pasar la noche en la calle, \q porque yo abría mis puertas al viajero.
es.R: Ningún forastero tuvo que dormir afuera en la calle. \q Siempre abrí mis puertas a los viajeros.

fr.L: L’étranger ne passait pas la nuit dans la rue ; \q j’ouvrais mes portes au voyageur.
fr.B: Aucun étranger n’avait à passer la nuit dans la rue, \q car j’ouvrais mes portes au voyageur.
fr.R: Aucun étranger n’a jamais dû dormir dehors dans la rue. \q J’ai toujours ouvert mes portes aux voyageurs.

sw.L: Mgeni hakulala njiani; \q milango yangu nilimfungulia msafiri.
sw.B: Hakuna mgeni aliyelazimika kulala barabarani, \q kwa maana nilimfungulia msafiri milango yangu.
sw.R: Hakuna mgeni aliyewahi kulala nje barabarani. \q Siku zote niliwafungulia wasafiri milango yangu.

vi.L: Khách lạ đã không ngủ đêm ngoài đường; \q các cửa tôi, tôi đã mở cho lữ khách.
vi.B: Không khách lạ nào phải qua đêm ngoài đường, \q vì tôi mở cửa nhà mình cho người lữ hành.
vi.R: Chưa từng có người khách lạ nào phải ngủ ngoài đường. \q Tôi luôn mở cửa đón khách đi đường.

ko.L: 나그네가 거리에서 밤을 지내지 않았고 \q 나는 길손에게 내 문들을 열었다.
ko.B: 나그네가 거리에서 밤을 보내야 하는 일이 없었으니 \q 내가 길손에게 내 문을 열어 주었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 낯선 사람이 거리에서 잠을 잔 적이 없었다. \q 나는 늘 길 가는 사람들에게 문을 열어 주었다.

pt.L: O estrangeiro não pernoitava na rua; \q eu abria as minhas portas ao viajante.
pt.B: Nenhum forasteiro precisava passar a noite na rua, \q pois eu abria as minhas portas ao viajante.
pt.R: Nenhum desconhecido jamais teve de dormir na rua. \q Eu sempre abria as minhas portas para os viajantes.

decisions.choice: hospitality to the stranger
decisions.reason: A traveler with nowhere to stay spent the night in the town square unless someone took him in (Genesis 19:2; Judges 19:15-21). Job swears that no one in his town ever had to.

decisions.choice: the traveler: the same consonants as "the path", read with different vowels
alternatives: I opened my doors to the road
decisions.reason: The vowels in the Hebrew text give "to the path" ('orach). The same letters read 'oreach mean "traveler", which fits the parallel with "sojourner", as the ancient translations understood it.

decisions.choice: sojourner: a foreigner living or staying away from home
decisions.reason: The word (ger) is someone from elsewhere, without land or family to protect him.

decisions.choice: sojourner (L), outsider (B), stranger (R)
decisions.reason: The usual renderings of ger in this translation; Readable "stranger" suits a traveler who has just arrived.

source.text: אִם־כִּסִּ֣יתִי כְאָדָ֣ם פְּשָׁעָ֑י לִטְמ֖וֹן בְּחֻבִּ֣י עֲוֺֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: If I have covered like humankind my transgressions, by hiding in my bosom my iniquity,

en.L: If I have covered my transgressions like humankind, \q by hiding my iniquity in my bosom,
en.B: If I have concealed my transgressions as people do, \q by hiding my guilt in my heart,
en.R: Have I hidden my sins the way people do, \q keeping my guilt a secret?

es.L: Si he encubierto como [la] humanidad mis transgresiones, \q escondiendo en mi seno mi iniquidad,
es.B: Si he ocultado mis transgresiones como hace la gente, \q escondiendo mi culpa en mi corazón,
es.R: ¿He escondido mis pecados como hace la gente, \q guardando en secreto mi culpa?

fr.L: Si j’ai couvert mes transgressions comme [le fait] l’humanité, \q en cachant mon iniquité dans mon sein,
fr.B: Si j’ai dissimulé mes transgressions comme le font les gens, \q en cachant ma faute dans mon cœur,
fr.R: Ai-je caché mes péchés comme les gens le font, \q en gardant ma faute secrète ?

sw.L: Ikiwa nimefunika makosa yangu kama wanadamu, \q kwa kuuficha uovu wangu kifuani mwangu,
sw.B: Ikiwa nimeficha makosa yangu kama watu wafanyavyo, \q kwa kuificha hatia yangu moyoni mwangu,
sw.R: Je, nimezificha dhambi zangu kama watu wanavyofanya, \q nikiiweka hatia yangu kuwa siri?

vi.L: Nếu tôi đã che giấu các vi phạm của tôi như loài người, \q bằng cách giấu tội ác tôi trong lòng,
vi.B: Nếu tôi đã che đậy các vi phạm của mình như người ta vẫn làm, \q bằng cách giấu tội lỗi trong lòng,
vi.R: Tôi có che giấu tội lỗi mình như người ta vẫn làm, \q giữ kín lỗi lầm mình không?

ko.L: 만일 내가 사람처럼 내 허물을 덮고 \q 내 죄악을 내 품에 숨겼다면,
ko.B: 만일 내가 사람들이 하듯 내 허물을 감추고 \q 내 죄를 마음속에 숨겼다면,
ko.R: 내가 다른 사람들처럼 내 죄를 감추고 \q 내 잘못을 숨겼느냐?

pt.L: Se encobri como os seres humanos as minhas transgressões, \q escondendo no meu peito a minha iniquidade,
pt.B: Se escondi as minhas transgressões como as pessoas fazem, \q ocultando a minha culpa no coração,
pt.R: Por acaso escondi os meus pecados como as pessoas fazem, \q guardando a minha culpa em segredo?

decisions.choice: like humankind: as people commonly do
decisions.reason: The word ('adam) can mean "humankind" or be the name Adam. As people do, Job could have hidden his faults; or he may mean "like Adam", who hid from God after his sin (Genesis 3:8-12).

decisions.choice: transgressions, iniquity: wrongs and the guilt for them
decisions.reason: The first word (pesha') is rebellion, breaking faith; the second ('avon) is wrongdoing and the guilt it brings. Job does not claim to be sinless (7:21; 13:26); he swears that he never hid what he did wrong.

decisions.choice: in my bosom: inside, out of sight
decisions.reason: The bosom (chov) is the inside of the garment at the chest, where something is kept hidden; it also stands for the inner self.

decisions.choice: my guilt in my heart
decisions.reason: Balanced says "guilt" for the iniquity one carries and "heart" for the bosom as the inner self (m2, m3).

source.text: כִּ֤י אֶֽעֱר֨וֹץ׀הָ֘מ֤וֹן רַבָּ֗ה וּבוּז־מִשְׁפָּח֥וֹת יְחִתֵּ֑נִי וָ֝אֶדֹּ֗ם לֹא־אֵ֥צֵא פָֽתַח׃

records.literal_gloss: because I dreaded [the] great multitude, and [the] contempt of clans terrified me, and I kept silent, not I went out [the] door,

en.L: because I dreaded the great multitude, \q and the contempt of clans terrified me, \q so that I kept silent and did not go out the door—
en.B: because I feared the great crowd \q and the contempt of the clans terrified me, \q so that I kept quiet and would not go out of my door—
en.R: Was I so afraid of what the crowd would say, \q so scared that the families around me would despise me, \q that I kept quiet and stayed inside?

es.L: porque temía a la gran multitud, \q y el desprecio de los clanes me aterraba, \q de modo que callé y no salí por la puerta—
es.B: porque temía a la gran muchedumbre \q y el desprecio de los clanes me aterraba, \q de modo que me quedé callado y no salía de mi puerta—
es.R: ¿Tenía tanto miedo de lo que diría la gente, \q tanto temor de que las familias de mi alrededor me despreciaran, \q que me quedé callado y no salí de casa?

fr.L: parce que je redoutais la grande foule, \q et que le mépris des clans m’épouvantait, \q de sorte que je me taisais et ne sortais pas de la porte —
fr.B: parce que je craignais la grande foule \q et que le mépris des clans me terrifiait, \q de sorte que je restais silencieux sans franchir ma porte —
fr.R: Avais-je si peur de ce que dirait la foule, \q si peur que les familles autour de moi me méprisent, \q que je me suis tu et suis resté enfermé chez moi ?

sw.L: kwa sababu niliuogopa umati mkubwa, \q na dharau ya koo ilinitisha, \q hata nikanyamaza, nisitoke mlangoni—
sw.B: kwa sababu niliuogopa umati mkubwa \q na dharau ya koo ilinitia hofu, \q hata nikanyamaza na sikutoka nje ya mlango wangu—
sw.R: Je, niliogopa sana watu watasema nini, \q nikaogopa kwamba familia zilizonizunguka zingenidharau, \q hata nikanyamaza na kukaa ndani?

vi.L: vì tôi đã sợ đám đông lớn, \q và sự khinh miệt của các gia tộc làm tôi kinh hãi, \q nên tôi im lặng và không ra khỏi cửa—
vi.B: vì tôi sợ đám đông lớn \q và sự khinh bỉ của các dòng họ làm tôi khiếp đảm, \q nên tôi lặng im và không bước ra khỏi cửa—
vi.R: Tôi có sợ người ta bàn tán, \q sợ các gia đình chung quanh khinh khi mình, \q đến nỗi im lặng và ở lì trong nhà không?

ko.L: 내가 큰 무리를 두려워했기 때문에, \q 족속들의 멸시가 나를 떨게 했기 때문에, \q 내가 잠잠하여 문밖으로 나가지 않았다면—
ko.B: 내가 큰 무리를 두려워하고 \q 집안들의 멸시가 무서워서 \q 입을 다물고 문밖으로 나가지 않았다면—
ko.R: 사람들이 뭐라고 할지 그렇게 두려웠느냐? \q 이웃 집안들이 나를 업신여길까 봐 겁이 나서 \q 입을 다물고 집 안에만 있었느냐?

pt.L: porque temi a grande multidão, \q e o desprezo dos clãs me aterrorizou, \q de modo que me calei e não saí pela porta—
pt.B: porque tive medo da grande multidão \q e o desprezo dos clãs me aterrorizou, \q de modo que fiquei calado e não quis sair de casa—
pt.R: Será que eu tinha tanto medo do que a multidão diria, \q tanto medo de que as famílias ao meu redor me desprezassem, \q que fiquei quieto e não saí de casa?

decisions.choice: the crowd, the contempt of clans: public disgrace
decisions.reason: Job pictures the shame a man would face if his hidden sin became known to the town and its families. He had been honored at the gate (29:7-10); he swears he never hid wrongdoing to keep that honor.

decisions.choice: dreaded, terrified: deep fear
decisions.reason: The first verb ('arats) means to tremble at, the second (chatat) to be shattered with fear.

decisions.choice: the oath breaks off
decisions.reason: The oath of verses 33-34 has no curse. Job breaks off and cries out for a hearing (verse 35), and the last oath and its curse come in verses 38-40.

decisions.choice: a dash that leads into verse 35
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced end the verse with a dash, since the oath has no curse and Job breaks off into his cry in verse 35 (m3).

source.text: מִ֤י יִתֶּן־לִ֨י׀שֹׁ֘מֵ֤עַֽ לִ֗י הֶן־תָּ֭וִי שַׁדַּ֣י יַעֲנֵ֑נִי וְסֵ֥פֶר כָּ֝תַ֗ב אִ֣ישׁ רִיבִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: Who will give to me [one] hearing me! Here [is] my mark; let Shaddai answer me! And [the] document [that] has written [the] man of my case!

en.L: Oh that I had one who would hear me! \q Here [is] my mark; let the Almighty answer me! \q And [oh for] the document my opponent at law has written!
en.B: Oh, that I had someone to hear me! \q Here is my signature; let the Almighty answer me! \q If only I had the charge my accuser has written!
en.R: I wish someone would listen to me! \q I have signed my name to all I have said. Now let God All-Powerful answer me! \q Let the one who accuses me write down the charges against me!

es.L: ¡Quién me diera uno que me oyera! \q Aquí [está] mi firma; ¡que el Todopoderoso me responda! \q ¡Y [ojalá tuviera] el documento que ha escrito mi adversario en el pleito!
es.B: ¡Ojalá tuviera a alguien que me escuchara! \q Aquí está mi firma; ¡que el Todopoderoso me responda! \q ¡Ojalá tuviera la acusación que ha escrito mi acusador!
es.R: ¡Quisiera que alguien me escuchara! \q He firmado con mi nombre todo lo que he dicho. ¡Ahora que el Dios Todopoderoso me responda! \q ¡Que el que me acusa escriba los cargos contra mí!

fr.L: Oh, si j’avais quelqu’un pour m’entendre ! \q Voici ma marque ; que le Tout-Puissant me réponde ! \q Et [oh, si j’avais] le document qu’a écrit mon adversaire en justice !
fr.B: Oh, si j’avais quelqu’un pour m’écouter ! \q Voici ma signature ; que le Tout-Puissant me réponde ! \q Si seulement j’avais l’acte d’accusation qu’a écrit mon accusateur !
fr.R: J’aimerais que quelqu’un m’écoute ! \q J’ai signé de mon nom tout ce que j’ai dit. Maintenant, que Dieu le Tout-Puissant me réponde ! \q Que celui qui m’accuse mette par écrit ses accusations contre moi !

sw.L: Laiti ningekuwa na mtu wa kunisikia! \q Tazama, [hii ni] alama yangu; Mwenyezi na anijibu! \q Na [laiti ningekuwa na] hati aliyoiandika mpinzani wangu katika kesi!
sw.B: Laiti ningekuwa na mtu wa kunisikiliza! \q Hii hapa sahihi yangu; Mwenyezi na anijibu! \q Laiti ningekuwa na hati ya mashtaka aliyoiandika anayenishtaki!
sw.R: Natamani mtu anisikilize! \q Nimetia sahihi yangu juu ya yote niliyosema. Sasa Mungu Mwenyezi na anijibu! \q Yule anayenishtaki na aandike mashtaka yake dhidi yangu!

vi.L: Ôi, ước gì có người nghe tôi! \q Đây [là] dấu của tôi; hãy để Đấng Toàn Năng trả lời tôi! \q Và [ước gì có] văn bản mà đối thủ trong vụ kiện của tôi đã viết!
vi.B: Ôi, ước gì có ai lắng nghe tôi! \q Đây là chữ ký của tôi; hãy để Đấng Toàn Năng trả lời tôi! \q Ước gì tôi có bản cáo trạng mà người cáo buộc tôi đã viết!
vi.R: Tôi ước gì có ai chịu nghe tôi! \q Tôi đã ký tên dưới mọi điều tôi nói. Giờ hãy để Đức Chúa Trời Toàn Năng trả lời tôi! \q Hãy để người cáo buộc tôi viết ra các tội trạng của tôi!

ko.L: 아, 내 말을 들어 줄 이가 있다면! \q 보라, 여기 내 서명이 [있다]. 전능자께서 내게 대답하시기를! \q 내 송사의 상대가 쓴 문서가 [내게 있다면]!
ko.B: 아, 내 말을 들어 줄 사람이 있으면 좋겠다! \q 여기 내 서명이 있으니 전능자께서 내게 대답하시기를 바란다! \q 나를 고소하는 자가 쓴 고소장이 내게 있으면 좋겠다!
ko.R: 누가 내 말을 들어 주면 좋겠다! \q 나는 내가 한 모든 말에 내 이름으로 서명했다. 이제 전능하신 하나님께서 내게 대답해 주시면 좋겠다! \q 나를 고소하는 이가 내 죄목을 적어 내면 좋겠다!

pt.L: Quem me dera ter quem me ouvisse! \q Eis a minha marca; que o Todo-Poderoso me responda! \q E [quem me dera] o documento que o meu adversário na causa escreveu!
pt.B: Ah, se eu tivesse alguém que me ouvisse! \q Aqui está a minha assinatura; que o Todo-Poderoso me responda! \q Se ao menos eu tivesse a acusação que o meu acusador escreveu!
pt.R: Como eu queria que alguém me escutasse! \q Assinei o meu nome embaixo de tudo o que eu disse. Agora, que o Deus Todo-Poderoso me responda! \q Que aquele que me acusa escreva as acusações contra mim!

decisions.choice: who will give: oh that, if only
decisions.reason: "Who will give ...?" is the Hebrew way of saying "if only" (6:8; 14:4; 23:3). Job used it when he wished his words were written in a document (19:23); now he wants the charges against him written.

decisions.choice: my mark: my signature
decisions.reason: The word (taw) is the name of the last letter of the Hebrew alphabet, which in old script was a cross-shaped mark (Ezekiel 9:4, 6). Here it is the mark a man puts to a document as his signature. Job signs his oath of innocence and hands it to the court.

decisions.choice: the man of my case: my opponent at law; most likely God himself
decisions.reason: "The man of my case" is the other party in a lawsuit. Job has asked God to state his charges (10:2; 13:22-23; 23:3-7), so the opponent is most likely God, whom he has just asked to answer; it could be any accuser. The text does not name him.

decisions.choice: the document: the written indictment
decisions.reason: A written document (sefer) could be a legal record, such as a certificate of divorce (Deuteronomy 24:1). Here it is the list of charges. Job is sure it would clear him (verse 36).

decisions.choice: I have signed my name to all I have said; God All-Powerful
decisions.reason: Readable says what the mark is and what it is put to (m2), and names Shaddai "God All-Powerful", as in every book.

decisions.choice: the charge (B), the charges (R); my accuser
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the document is (m4) and use "accuser" for "the man of my case", which keeps open who he is (m3).

decisions.choice: "mpinzani wangu katika kesi" (L), "anayenishtaki" (B, R) for "the man of my case"
decisions.reason: "Mshtaki" is the book's name for the Accuser of chapters 1-2; a verb phrase keeps Job's legal opponent apart from that figure.

decisions.choice: "나를 고소하는 자 / 이" for Job's opponent at law
decisions.reason: "고발자" is the book's name for the Accuser of chapters 1-2; "고소하다", the word for bringing a lawsuit, keeps Job's legal opponent apart from that figure.

decisions.choice: "quem me ouvisse" / "alguém que me ouvisse"; "que o Todo-Poderoso me responda"; "o meu adversário na causa" (L), "o meu acusador" (B), "aquele que me acusa" (R), lowercase
decisions.reason: As the English and the meaning decisions: the one Job wishes would hear him is not named, so Portuguese does not turn him into a title such as "o meu Defensor"; Shaddai is the one asked to answer, "o Todo-Poderoso" ("o Deus Todo-Poderoso" at Readable). The opponent at law is most likely God but may be any accuser (m3), so he is "o meu acusador" without a capital, as the English keeps "my accuser" open; the deity_pronoun spans of verse 37 follow the English. "Quem me dera" repeats the wish of 29:2 (m1).

source.text: אִם־לֹ֣א עַל־שִׁ֭כְמִי אֶשָּׂאֶ֑נּוּ אֶֽעֶנְדֶ֖נּוּ עֲטָר֣וֹת לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: If not on my shoulder I would carry it; I would bind it [as] crowns on me.

en.L: Surely on my shoulder I would carry it; \q I would bind it on me [as] a crown.
en.B: I would surely carry it on my shoulder; \q I would wear it like a crown.
en.R: I would proudly carry it on my shoulder. \q I would wear it on my head like a crown.

es.L: Ciertamente sobre mi hombro lo llevaría; \q me lo ceñiría [como] corona.
es.B: Sin duda lo llevaría sobre mi hombro; \q me lo pondría como una corona.
es.R: Lo llevaría con orgullo sobre mi hombro. \q Me lo pondría en la cabeza como una corona.

fr.L: Assurément, sur mon épaule je le porterais ; \q je me le ceindrais [comme] une couronne.
fr.B: Je le porterais assurément sur mon épaule ; \q je le mettrais comme une couronne.
fr.R: Je le porterais fièrement sur mon épaule. \q Je le mettrais sur ma tête comme une couronne.

sw.L: Hakika ningeibeba begani mwangu; \q ningeifunga juu yangu [kama] taji.
sw.B: Hakika ningeibeba begani mwangu; \q ningeivaa kama taji.
sw.R: Ningeibeba begani kwa fahari. \q Ningeivaa kichwani kama taji.

vi.L: Chắc chắn tôi sẽ vác nó trên vai; \q tôi sẽ buộc nó trên mình [như] mão miện.
vi.B: Chắc chắn tôi sẽ mang nó trên vai; \q tôi sẽ đội nó như một vương miện.
vi.R: Tôi sẽ hãnh diện vác nó trên vai. \q Tôi sẽ đội nó trên đầu như một vương miện.

ko.L: 내가 반드시 그것을 내 어깨에 메고 \q 그것을 면류관[처럼] 내게 매겠다.
ko.B: 나는 그것을 반드시 어깨에 메고 \q 면류관처럼 쓰겠다.
ko.R: 나는 그것을 자랑스럽게 어깨에 메겠다. \q 면류관처럼 머리에 쓰겠다.

pt.L: Certamente eu o carregaria sobre o meu ombro; \q eu o ataria a mim [como] uma coroa.
pt.B: Eu certamente o levaria sobre o ombro; \q eu o usaria como uma coroa.
pt.R: Eu carregaria esse documento com orgulho no ombro. \q Eu o usaria na cabeça como uma coroa.

decisions.choice: if not: surely
decisions.reason: "If not" is the form of an oath meaning "surely, I swear I would" (see verse 5).

decisions.choice: carry it on my shoulder, bind it on as a crown: display it openly, with honor
decisions.reason: Far from hiding the charges in shame (contrast verses 33-34), Job would wear them in public like a badge of honor, sure they would prove his innocence. The word for crown is plural (as in Zechariah 6:11), perhaps a crown made of several rings.

decisions.choice: proudly; on my head
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that carrying it would be a sign of honor (m2).

source.text: מִסְפַּ֣ר צְ֭עָדַי אַגִּידֶ֑נּוּ כְּמוֹ־נָ֝גִ֗יד אֲקָרֲבֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] number of my steps I would declare to him; like a prince I would approach him.

en.L: The number of my steps I would declare to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q like a prince I would approach {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: I would give {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} an account of every step I have taken; \q like a prince I would come near to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: I would tell {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} everything I have done. \q I would walk up to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} like a prince.

es.L: El número de mis pasos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} declararía; \q como un príncipe me acercaría a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Yo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} daría cuenta de cada paso que he dado; \q como un príncipe me acercaría a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Yo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} contaría todo lo que he hecho. \q Me presentaría ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} como un príncipe.

fr.L: Le nombre de mes pas, je le {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} déclarerais ; \q comme un prince je m’approcherais de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Je {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendrais compte de chacun de mes pas ; \q comme un prince je m’approcherais de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Je {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} raconterais tout ce que j’ai fait. \q Je m’avancerais vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} comme un prince.

sw.L: Hesabu ya hatua zangu ningemweleza; \q kama mkuu ningemkaribia.
sw.B: Ningempa hesabu ya kila hatua niliyopiga; \q kama mkuu ningemkaribia.
sw.R: Ningemweleza kila kitu nilichofanya. \q Ningemwendea kama kiongozi mwenye heshima.

vi.L: Số bước chân của tôi, tôi sẽ trình bày cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; \q như một vương hầu, tôi sẽ đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Tôi sẽ khai trình với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} từng bước tôi đã đi; \q như một vương hầu, tôi sẽ đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Tôi sẽ kể cho {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mọi điều tôi đã làm. \q Tôi sẽ ngẩng cao đầu bước đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như một vị vương hầu.

ko.L: 내 걸음의 수를 내가 그분께 아뢰고 \q 귀인처럼 그분께 나아가겠다.
ko.B: 나는 내가 걸어온 걸음을 하나하나 그분께 아뢰고 \q 귀인처럼 그분께 나아가겠다.
ko.R: 나는 내가 한 일을 다 그분께 말씀드리겠다. \q 귀인처럼 당당히 그분께 걸어가겠다.

pt.L: O número dos meus passos eu {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} declararia; \q como um príncipe eu me aproximaria {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.
pt.B: Eu {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} daria conta de cada passo que dei; \q como um príncipe eu chegaria perto {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.
pt.R: Eu contaria a {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} tudo o que fiz. \q Iria até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} como um príncipe.

decisions.choice: the number of my steps: answers verse 4
decisions.reason: Job asked whether God does not count all his steps (verse 4). Now he offers to give the count himself, a full account of his life.

decisions.choice: a prince: a leader, a man of rank
decisions.reason: The word (nagid) is a ruler or leader. Job would come before his judge with his head up, not as a guilty man cowering.

decisions.choice: him: the opponent of verse 35, most likely God
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers back to "the man of my case" in verse 35, read there as God (verse 35, m3).

decisions.choice: deity pronoun for him
decisions.reason: Since verse 35 reads Job's opponent as God, the pronouns take the deity pronoun setting; if he is another accuser, they would be plain "him".

decisions.choice: the land cries out: the land itself as a witness to wrong
decisions.reason: The ground cried out over Abel's blood (Genesis 4:10-11), and stones and beams cry out against those who build by violence (Habakkuk 2:11). Land taken unjustly or worked by oppressed laborers would cry out against its owner.

decisions.choice: the last oath
decisions.reason: After his signature (verse 35) Job makes one more oath, with its curse, about how he got and used his land. With it his speech ends.

decisions.choice: plowed fields; because of me
decisions.reason: Readable says "plowed fields" for "furrows" and supplies the reason they weep.

decisions.choice: its strength: what the land produces
decisions.reason: The land's "strength" (koach) is its yield, as in Genesis 4:12, where the ground will no longer give Cain its strength.

decisions.choice: made its owners breathe out their life: caused their death
decisions.reason: To make the life "breathe out" is to bring someone to their last breath. Job would have taken the land by killing or ruining its rightful owners, as Ahab did Naboth (1 Kings 21). The phrase could also mean making them gasp in despair (11:20; Jeremiah 15:9), or the owners could be the tenants who worked the land.

decisions.choice: without silver: without paying
decisions.reason: Silver was the money of the ancient world. To eat the produce without silver is to take it without paying the owner or the workers (Jeremiah 22:13).

decisions.choice: yield, crops; without payment
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the land's strength and the silver mean (m1, m3).

decisions.choice: thorns instead of wheat: the curse on the ground
decisions.reason: Job calls on his land the curse of Genesis 3:17-18, thorns in place of grain. If he had wronged the land, let it fail him.

decisions.choice: foul weeds: stinking weeds
decisions.reason: The word (bo'shah) comes from a verb meaning "to stink"; it names some foul-smelling weed whose kind is not known (compare the "stinking" wild grapes of Isaiah 5:2, 4).

decisions.choice: The words of Job are ended: a closing note
decisions.reason: These words close Job's speeches to his friends, like the note "The prayers of David son of Jesse are ended" with the same verb (Psalm 72:20). Job speaks again only briefly in answer to God (40:3-5; 42:1-6).

decisions.choice: then
decisions.reason: Balanced marks the start of the curse after the "if" clauses of verses 38-39.

decisions.choice: If I have, then; stinking weeds; This is the end of Job's words
decisions.reason: Readable gives the curse after its questions (verse 5, r-en-1), says "stinking weeds" (m2), and puts the closing note in plain words.
